key_insight: Agent-generated compiler patches often fix the reported LLVM example, but true success requires generalizing to the broader developer-intended optimization scope.
engineering_relevance: For compiler teams, this shows that patch-assistance systems should be judged by optimization generalization and not just by whether they repair a single missed case.
method: Built a benchmark from real-world LLVM missed-optimization issues
Compared agent-generated patches against developer patches by optimization scope
Added historical-knowledge augmentation using retrieval and distillation from prior LLVM optimization pull requests
evidence_signal: The study evaluates agent patches on real LLVM issues and reports that many patches only partially overlap with developer intent, while the knowledge-augmented approach improves alignment and practical applicability on real IR.
watch_item: A patch that works on the benchmark example may still be too narrow or over-generalize, so compiler validation must check behavior across similar IR patterns and downstream correctness.
paper_title: Understanding Agent-Based Patching of Compiler Missed Optimizations
